title: I directed AI agents through a whole horror game (night hotline, 51 calls, no engine). Free browser demo + what worked and what didn't
author: HeadSink1667
selftext:
The game is Probably the Pipes: you work a night hotline, people call about something in their house, you work out what it is from what they hear and tell them what to do. They do exactly what you say. Free demo in the browser: https://vit-ass.itch.io/probably-the-pipes

Trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cW_GAH49GJw

My part was the idea, every design call and the playtesting. The hands-on work (code, 51 call scripts in English and Russian, the archive, translation, builds, the trailer) was done by AI agents that I steered over a couple of weeks. Some things that came out of it:

**No engine.** Plain HTML/CSS/JS packed into one file. Agents are much better at reading and testing a codebase they can run headless than at clicking around an editor. There's an end-to-end suite that plays every call with every right and wrong answer, and nothing got merged without it passing.

**Image models are too clean for found photos.** The archive photos and the snapshots callers send were generated, but straight out of the model they looked like stock photos. What fixed it was a camera written in code: one fake button-phone sensor (soft lens, hand shake, gain noise, hard JPEG) applied the same way to every image. Same with the UI: generated icons looked obviously AI, so the icons and wallpaper are drawn in code as pixel art instead.

**Voices without voice actors or TTS.** Callers speak gibberish synthesised in code through a phone-line filter, and the words are subtitles. The background sounds are public-domain recordings, because synthesised scratching kept reading as an animal growl.

**Deduction balance is checked by a script, not by feel.** My complaint after the first playable version was that it was too easy: the interface was doing the noticing for the player. Now you tick the signs yourself, and a script counts how many archive entries are left after any two questions for every call (the target is 3 to 5), so no call collapses to one answer and none is a pure guess.

**The agent can't judge fear.** It can measure loudness, timing and whether a sound reads as a growl or a door, but whether a call is scary was always my job, and a lot of approved-by-metrics stuff got thrown out after I played it.

The itch page discloses all of this. Happy to answer questions about the workflow.
